first.rationale:
The two measurable regressions this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and those are causally linked: onboarding is upstream of activation, so a single onboarding intervention plausibly addresses both symptoms with one slot. Two independent inherited records (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on cutting signup fields) point the same direction, which is stronger evidence than any single record. Critically, the decline in onboarding completion suggests the prior gains have eroded or the flow has re-accreted friction since day 12/52 — so this is not blind replication but re-application to a changed baseline.

I am deliberately NOT leading with promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing, for two reasons. First, memory_73 carries an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, meaning the reported acquisition and revenue lift may be an artifact of cohort composition rather than a real price effect. That memory cannot be cited at face value. Second, and more importantly for the stated objective, discount-acquired accounts in a price-war context are exactly the accounts most likely to churn or to be re-poached by the next discounter; short-run acquisition lift can degrade the sustainable qualified revenue we are actually optimizing for. Matching a competitor's price is also the move most likely to trigger a margin spiral we do not control.

Verification spend: memory_73 because it is the one record with a known methodological flaw AND the one whose apparent conclusion most tempts us given current competitive pressure — highest value-of-information, since confirming the defect materially changes whether pricing is even a live option. memory_86 because it is the direct basis for my intended action and I want the original record to see the effect size, the population it held in, and whether the 'time-to-value' claim was measured or inferred. I am not verifying memory_31 despite it also supporting onboarding; it is the oldest record (day 12) and its corroborating role means a single confirmation of memory_86 is sufficient to proceed.

Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: all these memories predate the competitor's launch, so the environment that produced them no longer exactly obtains, and prior lifts may not reproduce. Standard experiment scale with a proper holdout, not a broad rollout — the inherited evidence justifies a real test, not a commitment. If verification shows memory_86's effect was small or narrowly scoped, I would downgrade to a small guarded test rather than switch to pricing.
